ground_truth.unit: change in the cabinet replacement rate (share of ministers, 0-1)
ground_truth.location: Table A1 (Tables for Figure 2), column Base Model, Failed coup attempt
ground_truth.context: Table A1 ("Failed coup attempts. Country fixed effects: Country-level results"), Base Model column; plotted in the left panel of Figure 2. Time-series cross-sectional OLS of the year-to-year cabinet replacement rate (one minus the cabinet-size-adjusted retention rate of ministers, from WhoGov, July to July) on a failed coup attempt indicator (Powell and Thyne data; a failed coup before 1 July counts in that year, one after 1 July in the following year), with logged GDP per capita and logged population (Penn World Table 9.0) lagged one year, country fixed effects and year fixed effects.  Sample: country-years of independent countries with a lagged Boix-Miller- Rosato democracy score of 0, 115 autocracies, 1967-2016.  Standard errors clustered by country.

i4r.notes: Blanket verdict (perfect reproduction).  R re-coding rows with o_coeff 0.10 (Table A1 Base or Purges MAs, which share the rounded value): 0.102 (0.031) and 0.129 (0.031).  Stata log: 0.0985 (0.0327).

ground_truth.unit: change in the probability of being purged next year
ground_truth.location: Table K1 (Table for Figure 3), column H2a: Experience, Failed coup attempt
ground_truth.context: Table K1, column H2a: Experience; Figure 3 left panel.  Linear probability model of whether a cabinet member is purged (absent from the cabinet the following year; reshuffles within the cabinet are not purges) on a failed coup attempt indicator, experience-group dummies (2-3, 4-6, over 6 years in cabinet; reference under 2 years), their interactions with the failed coup indicator, lagged logged GDP per capita and population, country and year fixed effects.  Minister-years in autocracies 1967-2016, excluding the leader and junior ministers or other low-ranking posts; standard errors clustered by country.  The failed coup coefficient is the effect for ministers with under two years of experience.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Country level: coupattempt_whogov used as delivered (taken to be the July-aligned WhoGov coup indicator); autocracy filter = one-year lag of democracy1 (BMR) == 0, years 1967-2016; country-FE sample N=3743 (paper 3,715), 93 failed coups (paper 95).

Leader-FE models (Table A2): one-year lags of democracy and controls taken within each leader spell (leader_cab_id), as if the panel were set on the leader id, so each spell's first year drops; N=3277 (paper 3,332). With country-panel lags (attempt-4) N was 3626 and the coefficients 0.062/0.064. Monarchy is (near-)collinear with leader FE, as the paper notes.

Individual level: experience model (H2a) does not drop junior ministers despite footnote 16; the sample is minister-years with non-missing importance tier, which reproduces the paper's coup-year count (1,926). Importance model drops the 6 tier-0 rows (coup-year count 1,925 as in the paper). Affiliation model drops party_group unknown/NA. N are ~380 below the paper's in each individual model.

Individual models: fixest drops pop_pwt_ln_lag (as supplied in the .rds) as collinear with country+year FE, even with collin.tol=1e-14; the paper reports a population coefficient. Lagged population was not reconstructed.
cell.notes: Independent reconstruction from the paper text with fixest: OLS of replacement_rateadj_minister on failed coup indicator + lagged log GDPpc and population (+ lagged monarchy/military/party dummies in Main), country or leader FE plus year FE, country-clustered SEs, singletons dropped. Individual LPMs of purged_y1 with fca x characteristic interactions, lagged GDPpc/pop, cubic in experience (not in the experience model), country+year FE, clustered by country; non-leader minister-years with lagged BMR democracy == 0, 1967-2016. Attempts 1-3 were exploratory (variable inspection and sample counts). Attempt 4 was the first estimating run; check_attempt reported all claims within tolerance, but the leader-FE sample size was well above the paper's, so the final run changes how lags are taken for the leader-FE models (and sets a tighter collinearity tolerance, which had no effect). No authors' scripts were opened.
